# SYX vocabulary — v5.0.0

The complete list of class and token names SYX declares in the installed version.
**A SYX name that is not on this page does not exist** — it compiles, and paints nothing.
Copy names exactly. `a-{x,y}` is shorthand for `a-x` and `a-y`.
Rules for using them: `AGENTS.md` (section *UI*) and `node_modules/syx-design-system/CONSUMING.md`.

**Themes** (import one: `import 'syx-design-system/themes/<name>.css'`): `example-01`, `example-02`, `example-03`, `example-04`, `example-05`, `example-06`, `syx-sketch`

**Layers**, in order: `syx.reset, syx.base, syx.tokens, syx.atoms, syx.molecules, syx.organisms, syx.app, syx.utilities`. App rules go in `syx.app`.

## Atoms (`atom-*`)

### `atom-avatar`
[scope: generic] A person's photo or, without one, their initials, at a fixed size: --sm (32px), md by default (40px), --lg (56px); --square for accounts and organisations. The photo is an <img class="atom-avatar__img"> cropped with object-fit: cover. Initials sit on bg-tertiary in secondary text, measured at 4.5:1 in contracts/contrast.json.
- modifiers: `atom-avatar--lg` `atom-avatar--sm` `atom-avatar--square`
- elements: `atom-avatar__img`
- a11y: Photo: alt with the person's name, or alt="" when the name is written right next to it. Initials alone do not say who it is: role="img" with aria-label="Full name"; next to the visible name, aria-hidden="true" instead. Not focusable — if it links to a profile, the link carries the name. In forced colours a border keeps the shape. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-avatar atom-avatar--lg"><img class="atom-avatar__img" src="img/avatar-demo.svg" alt="Ana López" width="56" height="56"></span><span class="atom-avatar" role="img" aria-label="Ana López">AL</span><span class="atom-avatar atom-avatar--sm atom-avatar--square" role="img" aria-label="Acme Inc.">AC</span>
```

### `atom-breadcrumb`
[scope: system-reusable] Ancestor trail for the current page. Use it when the user arrived at a page nested two or more levels deep and needs to climb back. Not a substitute for primary navigation, and pointless on a flat site.
- elements: `atom-breadcrumb__item` `atom-breadcrumb__link`
- states: `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Wrap the list in <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with an <ol>. The current page is plain text with aria-current="page", not a link. Separators are CSS and are not read. Links take the system focus ring. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"><ol class="atom-breadcrumb"><li class="atom-breadcrumb__item"><a class="atom-breadcrumb__link" href="/">Home</a></li><li class="atom-breadcrumb__item" aria-current="page">Tokens</li></ol></nav>
```

### `atom-btn`
[scope: system-reusable] The action trigger. --primary is the single dominant action of a decision context; --secondary/--tertiary/--quaternary step down from it; --danger marks a destructive action (delete, revoke) in the error state colour, never the brand; --filled makes any variant solid. Without a --size-* modifier a button is md, the same 48px height as a form field; --size-sm/--size-lg are 40/56px. Use --circle only for an icon-only control, and give it an aria-label. If the element navigates rather than acts, it is atom-link.
- modifiers: `atom-btn--circle` `atom-btn--danger` `atom-btn--filled` `atom-btn--has-icon` `atom-btn--primary` `atom-btn--quaternary` `atom-btn--secondary` `atom-btn--size-lg` `atom-btn--size-md` `atom-btn--size-sm` `atom-btn--tertiary`
- states: `:active` `:disabled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- composed of: `atom-icon`
- a11y: Native <button> with an explicit type ("button", or "submit" inside a form); an <a href> only when it navigates. Enter/Space come from the element. Icon-only (--circle) needs aria-label. Disable with the disabled attribute, not a class. Focus: system ring. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<button class="atom-btn atom-btn--primary atom-btn--size-md" type="button">Get started</button> <button class="atom-btn atom-btn--danger atom-btn--filled" type="button">Delete project</button>
```

### `atom-check`
[scope: system-reusable] Checkbox with a visible label, for choices that are independent of each other. The native input stays in the DOM and carries the state; the styling hangs off it. For one on/off setting that applies immediately, atom-switch reads better; for mutually exclusive options, atom-radio.
- elements: `atom-check__input` `atom-check__label`
- states: `:checked` `:disabled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Real <input type="checkbox"> inside the <label>, so the text is its name and the whole row toggles it. Space toggles. Related boxes go in a <fieldset> with a <legend>. The focus ring is drawn on the visible box. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<label class="atom-check"><input class="atom-check__input" type="checkbox" name="opt"><span class="atom-check__label">Include drafts</span></label>
```

### `atom-code`
[scope: domain-reusable] Code shown as content, on its own dark surface that ignores the page theme so a dark brand colour cannot make the syntax invisible. --inline for a fragment inside a sentence. The __tag/__attr/__val/__cls/__cmt elements are the syntax roles; nothing else colours code. Use in technical and documentation products, not as a generic panel.
- modifiers: `atom-code--inline`
- elements: `atom-code__attr` `atom-code__cls` `atom-code__cmt` `atom-code__tag` `atom-code__val`
- states: `:focus-visible`
- a11y: Static content in <pre><code>. A block that scrolls sideways needs tabindex="0" (and a label) so it can be scrolled from the keyboard. Colour is never the only cue. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<pre class="atom-code" tabindex="0" role="group" aria-label="Button markup"><code>&lt;<span class="atom-code__tag">button</span> <span class="atom-code__attr">class</span>=<span class="atom-code__val">"atom-btn"</span>&gt;</code></pre>
```

### `atom-feature-icon`
[scope: domain-reusable] Circular tinted container that gives an icon presence at the head of a card or list item. The shape is generic but the modifier set (--token, --mixin, --layer, --molecule, --organism) names SYX's own architecture: outside this domain only --primary carries meaning, so a new product needs its own modifiers rather than borrowing these. Always decorative — the meaning belongs to the text next to it.
- modifiers: `atom-feature-icon--layer` `atom-feature-icon--mixin` `atom-feature-icon--molecule` `atom-feature-icon--organism` `atom-feature-icon--primary` `atom-feature-icon--token`
- a11y: Decorative: always aria-hidden="true"; the meaning lives in the text next to it. Never focusable. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-feature-icon atom-feature-icon--token" aria-hidden="true"><span class="atom-icon atom-icon--lc-layers"></span></span>
```

### `atom-input`
[scope: system-reusable] The five canonical form primitives: .atom-label, .atom-input, .atom-textarea, .atom-select and .atom-input-wrapper. .atom-textarea shares the input's box, border, focus and states but not its fixed height: rows sets it, with a floor of two touch heights and vertical-only resize (textarea.atom-input still works). They are the raw controls only — validation state, message and character count live in mol-form-field, so use these bare only in a layout that handles its own error reporting.
- states: `:disabled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- composed of: `atom-label`
- a11y: Every control has a <label for> pointing at a unique id (ids repeat across a page more often than you think). Use the right type and autocomplete. .atom-select is a native <select>: keyboard and option list come from the browser. Inputs and selects are 48px tall at every width; a textarea is never shorter than two of those. Focus: system ring. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<label class="atom-label" for="form-email">Email</label><span class="atom-input-wrapper"><input class="atom-input" id="form-email" type="email" autocomplete="email"></span><label class="atom-label" for="form-plan">Plan</label><span class="atom-input-wrapper"><select class="atom-select" id="form-plan"><option>Free</option><option>Pro</option></select></span><label class="atom-label" for="form-notes">Notes</label><textarea class="atom-textarea" id="form-notes" rows="3"></textarea>
```

### `atom-icon`
[scope: system-reusable] Extends .atom-icon with 63 Lucide glyphs as --lc-* modifiers. The SVGs are embedded as data URIs, not linked: they are painted with mask-image, and a cross-origin mask is blocked, which left the site iconless over file://. Regenerated by scripts/build-lucide-tokens.js from img/icons/lucide/ — do not hand-edit the modifier block.
- modifiers: `atom-icon--lc-{activity,arrow-left,arrow-right,arrow-up,atom,award,book-open,bot,box,briefcase,check,check-circle,chevron-down,chevron-left,chevron-right,chevron-up,chevrons-down,chevrons-left,chevrons-right,code,coins,component,copy,corner-down-right,database,download,error,external-link,file-text,filter,git-branch,git-compare,github,home,info,layers,layout,link,mail,menu,minus,moon,package,palette,pencil,pie-chart,plus,rocket,search,settings,shield-check,success,sun,terminal,trash,user,users,warning,x,x-circle,zap}`
- composed of: `atom-icon`
- a11y: Decorative by default: aria-hidden="true". When it is the only content of a control, the control carries the aria-label, not the icon. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-icon atom-icon--lc-home atom-icon--color-primary" aria-hidden="true"></span>
```

### `atom-icon`
[scope: system-reusable] The icon primitive: a masked shape that inherits colour through --color-* modifiers and sizes through --sm/--md/--lg/--xl. This file holds the hand-drawn SYX set (arrows, bars, UI marks); the Lucide set extends the same class. An icon is decorative unless it is the only content of a control — mark it aria-hidden, or give the control an aria-label.
- modifiers: `atom-icon--arrow-default` `atom-icon--arrow-double` `atom-icon--color-black` `atom-icon--color-primary` `atom-icon--color-secondary` `atom-icon--color-state-ko` `atom-icon--color-state-ok` `atom-icon--color-state-warning` `atom-icon--color-white` `atom-icon--content-bars` `atom-icon--lg` `atom-icon--md` `atom-icon--rrss-email` `atom-icon--sm` `atom-icon--ui-cancel` `atom-icon--ui-exclamation` `atom-icon--ui-home` `atom-icon--ui-tick` `atom-icon--xl`
- a11y: Decorative by default: aria-hidden="true". When it is the only content of a control, the control carries the aria-label, not the icon. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-icon atom-icon--ui-tick atom-icon--color-state-ok atom-icon--md" aria-hidden="true"></span>
```

### `atom-label`
[scope: system-reusable] Caution: two different things claim .atom-label. This file styles a small scope marker (--scope-1/-2/-3, --primary); scss/atoms/_form.scss declares the same class as a form field label. Check which one the compiled CSS gives you before relying on either, and prefer atom-pill for a standalone tag.
- modifiers: `atom-label--primary` `atom-label--scope-1` `atom-label--scope-2` `atom-label--scope-3`
- a11y: Plain text, no role. If it marks a state, the words must say it. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-label atom-label--scope-1">Scope</span>
```

### `atom-link`
[scope: system-reusable] Inline navigational link. Use it when the element takes the user somewhere; if it performs an action, it is atom-btn regardless of how it looks. --primary is the styled variant with its own focus and hover treatment.
- modifiers: `atom-link--primary`
- states: `:active` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Native <a href>; if it performs an action it is a <button>. The text must make sense out of context ("Read the docs", not "here"). Every variant takes the system focus ring. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<a class="atom-link atom-link--primary" href="/docs">Read the docs</a>
```

### `atom-list`
[scope: system-reusable] Unstyled list plus two authored variants: --primary draws its own marker through ::before so the bullet colour follows the theme, --ordered numbers. Use it for real sequences and sets. Do not use it to lay out cards — that is a grid.
- modifiers: `atom-list--ordered` `atom-list--primary`
- a11y: Native <ul>/<ol> so the item count is announced. The --primary marker is CSS; WebKit drops list semantics when list-style is none, so add role="list" if that matters. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<ul class="atom-list atom-list--primary"><li class="atom-list__item">Primitives</li><li class="atom-list__item">Semantics</li></ul>
```

### `atom-pagination`
[scope: system-reusable] Page-by-page navigation over a finite, countable result set. Prev/next arrows come from the Lucide token system via ::before — mark the item --is-prev/--is-next and give the trigger an aria-label instead of visible text (a word overflows the square trigger). If the total is unknown or the list is a feed, this is the wrong control.
- elements: `atom-pagination__item` `atom-pagination__trigger`
- states: `:disabled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Wrap it in <nav aria-label="Pagination">; the current page carries aria-current="page". Prev/next are icon-only: aria-label ("Previous page", "Next page"), no visible text. <a href> for page URLs, <button type="button"> when script loads the results. A dead end uses --is-disabled plus disabled (button) or aria-disabled="true" (link). No JS required.
- usage:

```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination"><ul class="atom-pagination"><li class="atom-pagination__item atom-pagination__item--is-prev"><a class="atom-pagination__trigger" href="?p=1" aria-label="Previous page"></a></li><li class="atom-pagination__item"><a class="atom-pagination__trigger" href="?p=1">1</a></li><li class="atom-pagination__item atom-pagination__item--is-active"><a class="atom-pagination__trigger" href="?p=2" aria-current="page">2</a></li><li class="atom-pagination__item"><a class="atom-pagination__trigger" href="?p=3">3</a></li><li class="atom-pagination__item atom-pagination__item--is-next"><a class="atom-pagination__trigger" href="?p=3" aria-label="Next page"></a></li></ul></nav>
```

### `atom-pill`
[scope: system-reusable] Compact uppercase badge for a status, a category or a count. --success/--warning/--danger carry state; --neutral/--subtle/--dark are quiet; --primary/--secondary follow the brand. It is a label, not a button: if it is clickable, use atom-btn. Colour alone never conveys the state — the text has to say it too.
- modifiers: `atom-pill--danger` `atom-pill--dark` `atom-pill--neutral` `atom-pill--primary` `atom-pill--secondary` `atom-pill--subtle` `atom-pill--success` `atom-pill--warning`
- a11y: Static text, no role, not interactive (if it is clickable it is atom-btn). The state is in the words, never only in the colour. A count that updates needs an aria-live container. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-pill atom-pill--success">Stable</span>
```

### `atom-progress`
[scope: generic] A progress bar on the native <progress>: with value it is determinate, without value it is indeterminate (:indeterminate) and a segment sweeps the track. The fill is primary-strong, measured at 3:1 against the page and the track (WCAG 1.4.11). Under reduced motion the indeterminate bar stops moving and shows static stripes. For an unknown wait with no bar, use atom-spinner.
- a11y: Native <progress>: role progressbar, value and max come from the browser; remove value for indeterminate. It needs a name — <label for> on a unique id, or aria-label. The text inside <progress> is the fallback, not the name. Not focusable. Reduced motion: static stripes instead of the sweep. Forced colours: framed track, Highlight fill. No JS — the app updates value.
- usage:

```html
<label class="atom-label" for="pg-upload">Uploading report.pdf</label><progress class="atom-progress" id="pg-upload" value="40" max="100">40%</progress><label class="atom-label" for="pg-sync">Syncing contacts</label><progress class="atom-progress" id="pg-sync">Syncing…</progress>
```

### `atom-radio`
[scope: system-reusable] One choice out of a mutually exclusive set. Only meaningful in a group sharing a name, and the group needs a fieldset with a legend to be announced as a group. For independent choices use atom-check.
- elements: `atom-radio__input` `atom-radio__label`
- states: `:checked` `:disabled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Real <input type="radio"> inside the <label>, one name per group, the group in <fieldset><legend>. Arrow keys move the choice (browser). No JS.
- usage:

```html
<label class="atom-radio"><input class="atom-radio__input" type="radio" name="theme" value="dark"><span class="atom-radio__label">Dark</span></label>
```

### `atom-skeleton`
[scope: generic] A placeholder with the shape of the content that is on its way: --text (a line; the last of several stops at 60%), --circle (avatar size) and --block. A shimmer sweeps it; under reduced motion it stays flat. It is decoration: hide it from assistive technology and say what is loading in text.
- modifiers: `atom-skeleton--block` `atom-skeleton--circle` `atom-skeleton--text`
- a11y: aria-hidden="true" on every skeleton and aria-busy="true" on the container that will be filled; remove aria-busy when the content lands. Say what is loading with text in a role="status" outside the busy container (a busy region may hold its own announcements back). Never focusable. Reduced motion: no shimmer. Forced colours: a border keeps the shape. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<p class="syx-sr-only" role="status">Loading profile…</p><div class="layout-cluster layout-cluster--md" aria-busy="true"><span class="atom-skeleton atom-skeleton--circle" aria-hidden="true"></span><div class="layout-stack layout-stack--xs syx-flex-1" aria-hidden="true"><span class="atom-skeleton atom-skeleton--text"></span><span class="atom-skeleton atom-skeleton--text"></span></div></div>
```

### `atom-spinner`
[scope: generic] A busy indicator for a wait of unknown length: a ring drawn on ::before, so the text does not spin. The text lives in __label, visually hidden by default and shown with --with-label. --sm, md by default, --lg. Under reduced motion it spins three times slower instead of stopping, because a still ring says nothing. If the wait has a known end, use atom-progress.
- modifiers: `atom-spinner--lg` `atom-spinner--sm` `atom-spinner--with-label`
- elements: `atom-spinner__label`
- a11y: Always a text in __label: the ring alone says nothing to a screen reader. role="status" announces it politely without moving focus; a live region inserted with its text already inside may not be read, so insert it empty and set the text after, or announce from a status region that already exists. Not focusable. Reduced motion: slower, not stopped. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<span class="atom-spinner" role="status"><span class="atom-spinner__label">Loading results…</span></span><span class="atom-spinner atom-spinner--lg atom-spinner--with-label" role="status"><span class="atom-spinner__label">Saving changes…</span></span>
```

### `atom-stat`
[scope: system-reusable] One number plus the word that explains it, sized to be read across the page. Use it for a figure that supports an argument. It stops working the moment there are many: four is a row of evidence, twelve is a table.
- modifiers: `atom-stat--accent` `atom-stat--light`
- elements: `atom-stat__label` `atom-stat__number`
- a11y: Static. The explaining word is visible text next to the number; if the number animates, the final value is in the DOM from the start. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="atom-stat"><span class="atom-stat__number">19</span><span class="atom-stat__label">Atoms</span></div>
```

### `atom-switch`
[scope: system-reusable] Binary setting that takes effect on the spot, with no submit step. If the change only lands when a form is sent, the user expects a checkbox — use atom-check.
- elements: `atom-switch__input` `atom-switch__label` `atom-switch__slider`
- states: `:checked` `:disabled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> inside the <label>; the drawn track is aria-hidden. Space toggles and the on/off state is announced from the checkbox. It applies at once, so say what changed if it is not visible. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<label class="atom-switch"><input class="atom-switch__input" type="checkbox" role="switch"><span class="atom-switch__slider" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="atom-switch__label">Dark mode</span></label>
```

### `atom-table`
[scope: system-reusable] Tabular data — rows that compare along shared columns. --resp goes on the wrapper <div> (with __container), never on the <table>: overflow has no effect on a table box, so the page itself scrolled sideways. The table keeps a min-width floor so it scrolls instead of collapsing, and --is-stick-thead pins the header. Never for layout: if the cells do not share a meaning down the column, it is not a table.
- modifiers: `atom-table--is-stick-thead` `atom-table--primary` `atom-table--resp`
- elements: `atom-table__container` `atom-table__td` `atom-table__th`
- states: `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Native <table> with <th scope> headers; name it with <caption> or aria-label. With --resp the scrolling element is the wrapper <div>: give it role="region", an aria-label and tabindex="0" so it can be scrolled from the keyboard (it takes the system focus ring). No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="atom-table__container atom-table--resp" role="region" aria-label="Semantic tokens" tabindex="0"><table class="atom-table atom-table--primary"><thead><tr><th class="atom-table__th" scope="col">Token</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="atom-table__td">--semantic-color-text-primary</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
```

### `atom-title`
[scope: system-reusable] Headline styling detached from document level: --h1 to --h6 set size only. Pick the heading tag from the document outline and the modifier from the visual hierarchy — they do not have to match, and forcing them to is how outlines get broken to win a size.
- modifiers: `atom-title--h1` `atom-title--h2` `atom-title--h3` `atom-title--h4` `atom-title--h5` `atom-title--h6`
- a11y: Pick the heading level from the document outline; the modifier only sets the size. Never skip levels to get a size. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<h2 class="atom-title atom-title--h3">Token architecture</h2>
```

### `atom-txt`
[scope: system-reusable] Body copy. --primary only sets the bottom margin of a paragraph in a stack; colour, size and measure come from the semantic type scale, so there is nothing to configure here. If a paragraph needs to look secondary, that is a token role, not a modifier of this atom.
- modifiers: `atom-txt--primary`
- a11y: Static body text. No role, no JS.
- usage:

```html
<p class="atom-txt atom-txt--primary">SYX is a token-driven, native SCSS design system.</p>
```

## Molecules (`mol-*`)

### `mol-alert`
[scope: generic] A status message inside the page flow: --info, --success, --warning, --error. The state colours the accent rule and the title (state-*-text, measured at 4.5:1 on its background); the body stays in primary text. Use role="status" for information and role="alert" only for errors that need attention now; the role must be in the DOM before the text arrives.
- modifiers: `mol-alert--error` `mol-alert--info` `mol-alert--success` `mol-alert--warning`
- elements: `mol-alert__body` `mol-alert__title`
- a11y: role="status" (polite) for information; role="alert" only for an error that needs attention now. The live region must be in the DOM before its text changes. Not focusable. No JS for a static message.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-alert mol-alert--warning" role="status"><p class="mol-alert__title">Your plan expires in 3 days</p><p class="mol-alert__body">Renew it to keep your history.</p></div>
```

### `mol-btn-group`
[scope: system-reusable] Row of related actions with the standard gap between them, wrapping on narrow viewports. It arranges buttons; it does not rank them — the hierarchy is the buttons' own modifiers, and a group where every button is --primary has no primary action. .cont-set-btn is a deprecated alias.
- a11y: Every button inside has an explicit type. As a plain row it needs no role; if it behaves as one control, it becomes role="toolbar" with an aria-label and arrow-key navigation in script. No JS otherwise.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-btn-group"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--primary atom-btn--size-md" type="button">Save</button><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md" type="button">Cancel</button></div>
```

### `mol-card`
[scope: generic] The general-purpose surface for product screens: optional __media, __header (with __title and maybe a pill or an action), __body and __footer, spaced by the card itself. Bordered by default; --elevated swaps the border for a shadow and --flat drops both on bg-secondary. For a whole-card link, put .mol-card__link on the title's <a>: its ::after covers the card, the focus ring surrounds the card, and any other control inside stays clickable above it. Body text is text-secondary, measured on both backgrounds.
- modifiers: `mol-card--elevated` `mol-card--flat`
- elements: `mol-card__body` `mol-card__footer` `mol-card__header` `mol-card__link` `mol-card__media` `mol-card__title`
- states: `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: <article> when the card makes sense on its own (an item in a list), <div> otherwise; the page decides the heading level of __title. Whole-card link: the <a class="mol-card__link"> goes in the title so its name is the title, never an <a> wrapping the whole card (its name would be all the text). The ring is drawn on the link's ::after, around the card. Other controls inside are raised above the link area. Forced colours: every variant gets a visible frame. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<article class="mol-card"><header class="mol-card__header"><h3 class="mol-card__title">Storage</h3><span class="atom-pill atom-pill--neutral">80% used</span></header><div class="mol-card__body"><p>You have used 8 of 10 GB. Old exports are deleted after 30 days.</p></div><footer class="mol-card__footer"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-sm" type="button">Manage storage</button></footer></article><article class="mol-card mol-card--elevated"><h3 class="mol-card__title"><a class="mol-card__link" href="#billing">Billing</a></h3><div class="mol-card__body"><p>Invoices, payment method and tax details.</p></div></article>
```

### `mol-code-snippet`
[scope: domain-reusable] A code block with a header that judges it: --ok for the correct way, --ko for the rejected one, --neutral for a plain sample. Built for teaching a rule by showing both sides, so a lone --neutral snippet is usually just atom-code. The label has to state the verdict in words — the colour is not the message.
- modifiers: `mol-code-snippet--ko` `mol-code-snippet--neutral` `mol-code-snippet--ok`
- elements: `mol-code-snippet__body` `mol-code-snippet__filename` `mol-code-snippet__header` `mol-code-snippet__label`
- states: `:focus-visible`
- a11y: The header label states the verdict in words. A body that scrolls sideways needs tabindex="0". No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-code-snippet mol-code-snippet--ok"><div class="mol-code-snippet__header"><span class="mol-code-snippet__label">Correct</span></div><pre class="mol-code-snippet__body atom-code" tabindex="0" role="group" aria-label="Correct example"><code>color: var(--semantic-color-text-primary);</code></pre></div>
```

### `mol-dialog`
[scope: generic] A modal on the native <dialog>. The usage is the closed markup: open it from script with dialog.showModal() — never with the open attribute, which gives no top layer, no focus trap, no Escape and no inert page. Enters with @starting-style; no transition under reduced motion. For destructive confirmations use role="alertdialog", point aria-describedby at the body and autofocus the cancel button.
- elements: `mol-dialog__body` `mol-dialog__footer` `mol-dialog__inner` `mol-dialog__title`
- a11y: Native <dialog> opened with showModal() — the browser gives top layer, focus trap, Escape and an inert page; the open attribute gives none of it. aria-labelledby → title, aria-describedby → body. Destructive confirmation: role="alertdialog" and autofocus on Cancel. <form method="dialog"> buttons close it and return their value; focus goes back to the opener. JS: the showModal() call.
- usage:

```html
<dialog class="mol-dialog" role="alertdialog" aria-labelledby="dlg-title" aria-describedby="dlg-desc"><form method="dialog" class="mol-dialog__inner"><h2 class="mol-dialog__title" id="dlg-title">Delete “Report”?</h2><p class="mol-dialog__body" id="dlg-desc">Files and history will be lost.</p><div class="mol-dialog__footer"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md" value="cancel" autofocus>Cancel</button><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--danger atom-btn--filled atom-btn--size-md" value="ok">Delete</button></div></form></dialog>
```

### `mol-disclosure`
[scope: generic] Show and hide on native <details>/<summary>: keyboard and expanded state come from the browser. Several with the same name="" form an exclusive accordion. Never replace <summary> with a <div>.
- elements: `mol-disclosure__content` `mol-disclosure__summary`
- states: `:focus-visible`
- a11y: Native <details>/<summary>: Enter/Space toggle and the expanded state is announced by the browser. No interactive content inside <summary>, and never a <div> in its place. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<details class="mol-disclosure" name="faq"><summary class="mol-disclosure__summary">Can I change plans?</summary><div class="mol-disclosure__content">Yes, whenever you want.</div></details>
```

### `mol-empty-state`
[scope: generic] What shows where there is nothing yet — an empty list, a search with no results: a decorative __icon, a __title that says what is going on, a __text that says why or what to do, and __actions with the way out. Centred, because it takes the place of the missing content. --bordered frames it with a dashed border for a zone that waits for content (a drop target, an empty column). Title and text are measured at 4.5:1.
- modifiers: `mol-empty-state--bordered`
- elements: `mol-empty-state__actions` `mol-empty-state__icon` `mol-empty-state__text` `mol-empty-state__title`
- a11y: The icon is decorative (aria-hidden="true"); the title says what happened, at the heading level the page needs. If the empty state appears after an action (filter, search), announce it: put it inside a role="status" container that already existed, or move focus to the title (tabindex="-1") when it replaces what had focus. Not focusable itself; its buttons are. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-empty-state mol-empty-state--bordered"><span class="mol-empty-state__icon" aria-hidden="true"><span class="atom-icon atom-icon--lc-search atom-icon--lg"></span></span><h3 class="mol-empty-state__title">No projects match “q4”</h3><p class="mol-empty-state__text">Try another word, or clear the filters to see every project.</p><div class="mol-empty-state__actions"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md" type="button">Clear filters</button><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--primary atom-btn--filled atom-btn--size-md" type="button">New project</button></div></div>
```

### `mol-feature-card`
[scope: system-reusable] One capability, stated once, inside a set whose members carry equal weight. It composes atom-feature-icon, a title and a body, and every card in the grid looks the same on purpose — the design asserts that no item outranks another. Wrong choice when the content has editorial hierarchy, when one item must dominate the others, or when the card carries article metadata (author, date, read time): use a layout that ranks, not a grid that levels.
- elements: `mol-feature-card__body` `mol-feature-card__cta` `mol-feature-card__title`
- states: `:hover`
- a11y: <article> with a real heading. Only the CTA link is focusable (system ring); the card mirrors it with :focus-within. Icon aria-hidden. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<article class="mol-feature-card"><span class="atom-feature-icon atom-feature-icon--token" aria-hidden="true"></span><h3 class="mol-feature-card__title">Token system</h3><p class="mol-feature-card__body">Four tiers, one direction.</p><a class="mol-feature-card__cta atom-link" href="/tokens">Learn more</a></article>
```

### `mol-form-field-set`
[scope: system-reusable] Stacks related mol-form-field with the standard gap; --inline flows them in a row. Grouping for rhythm only — if the fields answer one question together, they also need a real fieldset and legend so the grouping is announced, not just seen.
- modifiers: `mol-form-field-set--inline`
- composed of: `mol-form-field`
- a11y: Visual grouping only. If the fields answer one question together, wrap them in <fieldset><legend> so the group is announced. Each field keeps its own <label>. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-form-field-set mol-form-field-set--inline"><div class="mol-form-field"><label class="atom-label" for="ffs-given">First name</label><input class="atom-input" id="ffs-given" type="text" autocomplete="given-name"></div><div class="mol-form-field"><label class="atom-label" for="ffs-family">Last name</label><input class="atom-input" id="ffs-family" type="text" autocomplete="family-name"></div></div>
```

### `mol-form-field`
[scope: system-reusable] The complete field: label, control, state and message. Use this rather than the bare atoms whenever the field can be wrong — --is-error/--is-success/--is-warning set the state and __msg carries the explanation. Wire the message with aria-describedby and mark the invalid control aria-invalid; the modifier paints, it does not announce. A textarea with maxlength can carry an optional __count: js/syx-char-count.js writes what is left (data-template, in the page's language), adds is-limit at the limit and announces it once typing pauses; without JS the markup text stays.
- modifiers: `mol-form-field--has-select` `mol-form-field--is-error` `mol-form-field--is-success` `mol-form-field--is-warning`
- elements: `mol-form-field__count` `mol-form-field__live` `mol-form-field__msg`
- states: `.is-limit`
- composed of: `atom-input` `atom-label` `atom-select` `atom-textarea`
- a11y: <label for> on a unique id. On error: aria-invalid="true" on the control and aria-describedby pointing at __msg — the modifier paints, the attributes announce. Character count: the textarea names __count in aria-describedby (heard on focus) and keeps maxlength; js/syx-char-count.js (no dependencies) adds a role="status" region that says what is left after a pause, never on every key. Validation itself is the app's.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-form-field mol-form-field--is-error"><label class="atom-label" for="ff-email">Email</label><input class="atom-input" id="ff-email" type="email" autocomplete="email" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="ff-email-msg"><span class="mol-form-field__msg" id="ff-email-msg">Enter a valid address.</span></div><div class="mol-form-field"><label class="atom-label" for="ff-bio">Short bio</label><textarea class="atom-textarea" id="ff-bio" rows="3" maxlength="160" aria-describedby="ff-bio-count"></textarea><span class="mol-form-field__count" id="ff-bio-count" data-template="{n} characters left">Up to 160 characters</span></div>
```

### `mol-label-group`
[scope: system-reusable] Row of labels or pills sharing one gap, wrapping when it must. Use it for a tag list or a set of markers on one line. .cont-set-label is a deprecated alias.
- a11y: Container only. If the labels are a list, use <ul role="list">. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-label-group"><span class="atom-pill atom-pill--neutral">SCSS</span><span class="atom-pill atom-pill--neutral">Tokens</span></div>
```

### `mol-menu`
[scope: generic] A button that opens a list of actions ("More", "Actions", a table row's menu). The __list is popover="auto": top layer, light dismiss and Escape come from the browser, and popovertarget opens it even without script. js/syx-menu.js adds the WAI-ARIA menu button keyboard, keeps aria-expanded true to the real state and places the list under the button (above if it does not fit), aligned to its start. __item--danger for destructive actions, aria-disabled="true" for an action that exists but cannot run now, __separator between groups. To navigate to other pages this is not a menu: use a list of links or mol-disclosure.
- elements: `mol-menu__item` `mol-menu__list` `mol-menu__separator` `mol-menu__trigger`
- states: `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Button: aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded, aria-controls and popovertarget pointing at the list. List: role="menu" with aria-labelledby → button; each option role="menuitem" (a <button>, or an <a> for a link). Keyboard from js/syx-menu.js (no dependencies): ↓/Enter/Space open on the first option, ↑ on the last; ↑↓ move with wrap, Home/End, a letter jumps to the next option starting with it, Escape and Tab close and return focus to the button; activating an option closes the menu. aria-disabled options stay focusable but do nothing. Without JS, popovertarget still opens and closes it and Tab reaches the options.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-menu"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md mol-menu__trigger" type="button" id="menu-actions-btn" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="menu-actions" popovertarget="menu-actions">Actions <span class="atom-icon atom-icon--lc-chevron-down atom-icon--sm" aria-hidden="true"></span></button><div class="mol-menu__list" id="menu-actions" role="menu" aria-labelledby="menu-actions-btn" popover="auto"><button class="mol-menu__item" type="button" role="menuitem">Rename</button><button class="mol-menu__item" type="button" role="menuitem">Duplicate</button><button class="mol-menu__item" type="button" role="menuitem" aria-disabled="true">Move to folder</button><div class="mol-menu__separator" role="separator"></div><button class="mol-menu__item mol-menu__item--danger" type="button" role="menuitem">Delete</button></div></div>
```

### `mol-tabs`
[scope: generic] Tabbed panels whose state lives in ARIA: the active tab has aria-selected="true", hidden panels carry hidden. Behaviour (click, arrows, Home/End, roving tabindex) comes from js/syx-tabs.js, dependency-free: import 'syx-design-system/js/syx-tabs.js' wires every tablist present on load, and initTabs(root) from the same module wires markup rendered later. Without it the selected panel shows and the tabs never switch.
- elements: `mol-tabs__list` `mol-tabs__panel` `mol-tabs__tab`
- states: `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: role tablist/tab/tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby; hidden on inactive panels; type="button" on every tab; panels focusable (tabindex="0"). Arrows, Home/End and roving tabindex come from js/syx-tabs.js (no dependencies); without it every panel stays reachable.
- usage:

```html
<div class="mol-tabs"><div class="mol-tabs__list" role="tablist" aria-label="Settings"><button class="mol-tabs__tab" type="button" role="tab" id="tab-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="panel-1">Profile</button><button class="mol-tabs__tab" type="button" role="tab" id="tab-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="panel-2" tabindex="-1">Notifications</button></div><div class="mol-tabs__panel" role="tabpanel" id="panel-1" aria-labelledby="tab-1" tabindex="0">Profile settings</div><div class="mol-tabs__panel" role="tabpanel" id="panel-2" aria-labelledby="tab-2" tabindex="0" hidden>Notification settings</div></div>
```

### `mol-toast`
[scope: generic] Ephemeral notifications in a corner that confirm what just happened ("Saved", "Link copied") without interrupting or taking focus. The .mol-toast container is fixed and stacks __item elements (--info, --success, --warning, --error colour only the accent rule; text stays primary). js/syx-toast.js: showToast('Saved', { tone, duration }) creates one, announces only its text through the container's __live region (role="status"), removes it after 6 s by default and pauses the countdown while the pointer or focus is on it or the tab is hidden; duration: 0 keeps it until dismissed. A button with data-syx-toast="Text" shows one without writing JS. Never the only place for something that must be read or done: an error that needs attention is mol-alert with role="alert".
- elements: `mol-toast__close` `mol-toast__item` `mol-toast__live` `mol-toast__text`
- states: `.is-leaving` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: The container holds a __live element with role="status" that exists before any text arrives; js/syx-toast.js writes only the message there, so the close button is not read out. Focus never moves to a toast; its close button (aria-label, 32px target) is reachable with Tab, and closing it returns focus to where the user came from. The countdown pauses on hover, on focus and while the tab is hidden (WCAG 2.2.1); duration: 0 disables it. Reduced motion: no slide or fade. Without JS a static toast stays and its button does nothing.
- usage:

```html
<button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md" type="button" data-syx-toast="Link copied to the clipboard" data-syx-toast-tone="success">Copy link</button><div class="mol-toast" data-dismiss-label="Dismiss notification"><p class="mol-toast__live" role="status"></p><div class="mol-toast__item mol-toast__item--info"><p class="mol-toast__text">3 files moved to Archive</p><button class="mol-toast__close" type="button" aria-label="Dismiss notification"><span class="atom-icon atom-icon--lc-x atom-icon--sm" aria-hidden="true"></span></button></div></div>
```

### `mol-tooltip`
[scope: generic] A short sentence that describes a control, on the Popover API: the __bubble is popover="hint" (browsers that do not know hint treat it as manual), so it sits in the top layer above any overflow or z-index. js/syx-tooltip.js opens it on keyboard focus and on hover, keeps it while the pointer is over the control or the bubble, closes it on Escape, blur or leaving, and places it above the control — below if it does not fit — never over it. Position comes from script because CSS anchor positioning is not in the support floor. Colours are text-primary and bg-primary swapped, so contrast holds wherever primary text does. Plain text only.
- elements: `mol-tooltip__bubble`
- a11y: aria-describedby on the control points at the bubble, which carries role="tooltip"; for an icon-only control the bubble is its name, so use aria-labelledby instead. WCAG 1.4.13: appears on focus and hover, hoverable (the pointer can move onto it), dismissed by Escape without moving focus or pointer, never covers the control. Nothing focusable inside. Never on a disabled control (no focus, no pointer events). JS: js/syx-tooltip.js (no dependencies); without it the bubble never opens, so do not put essential information only there.
- usage:

```html
<span class="mol-tooltip"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md" type="button" aria-describedby="tip-share">Share</button><span class="mol-tooltip__bubble" id="tip-share" role="tooltip" popover="hint">Copies a view-only link to the clipboard</span></span>
```

## Organisms (`org-*`)

### `org-app-shell`
[scope: generic] The frame of an application screen (settings, a dashboard, a console): __header on top, a __sidebar with the section navigation and __main, laid out with named grid areas. Below 50em everything stacks and the sidebar's __nav becomes a horizontally scrolling row — no drawer, no JS; from 50em the sidebar is a column beside the content. --full fills the viewport and keeps the header and the sidebar in place while the content scrolls. The current section is painted from aria-current="page" (colour, background and an inline-start rule that survives forced colours). Inside __main, layout-stack and layout-cluster arrange sections and actions.
- modifiers: `org-app-shell--full`
- elements: `org-app-shell__actions` `org-app-shell__brand` `org-app-shell__header` `org-app-shell__link` `org-app-shell__main` `org-app-shell__nav` `org-app-shell__sidebar`
- states: `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- a11y: Three landmarks a screen-reader user jumps between: <header>, <nav aria-label> and <main> — one <main> per page (the docs demo nests it inside the docs page's own, which a real app never does). The current section carries aria-current="page"; the CSS paints it from that attribute. Sidebar links are 44px tall; the scrolling row on small screens is padded so the focus ring is never clipped. No JS.
- usage:

```html
<div class="org-app-shell"><header class="org-app-shell__header"><span class="org-app-shell__brand">Acme Console</span><div class="org-app-shell__actions"><span class="atom-avatar atom-avatar--sm" role="img" aria-label="Signed in as Ana López">AL</span></div></header><nav class="org-app-shell__sidebar" aria-label="Sections"><ul class="org-app-shell__nav"><li><a class="org-app-shell__link" href="#overview">Overview</a></li><li><a class="org-app-shell__link" href="#settings" aria-current="page">Settings</a></li><li><a class="org-app-shell__link" href="#billing">Billing</a></li></ul></nav><main class="org-app-shell__main"><div class="layout-stack"><h2 class="atom-title atom-title--h4">Settings</h2><p class="atom-txt">Workspace name, members and notifications.</p><div class="layout-cluster layout-cluster--end"><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--secondary atom-btn--size-md" type="button">Cancel</button><button class="atom-btn atom-btn--primary atom-btn--filled atom-btn--size-md" type="button">Save</button></div></div></main></div>
```

### `org-site-header`
[scope: domain-reusable] Mobile-first sticky header with a hamburger that opens a nav drawer over an overlay. The header, drawer and overlay are three sibling elements and all three must be present; the burger names the drawer with aria-controls. js/syx-site-nav.js (no dependencies) toggles [data-nav-open] on <body> and manages focus and inert. The __theme-select and __darkmode controls are documentation-site furniture — a product that ships no theme picker should drop them rather than hide them.
- elements: `org-site-header__actions` `org-site-header__brand` `org-site-header__burger` `org-site-header__burger-line` `org-site-header__darkmode` `org-site-header__nav` `org-site-header__theme-select`
- states: `.is-scrolled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- composed of: `atom-btn` `atom-icon` `atom-select`
- a11y: <header> with a labelled desktop <nav> and a separately labelled drawer <nav>. Burger: <button type="button"> with aria-controls (drawer id), aria-expanded and aria-label. js/syx-site-nav.js: closed drawer is inert (and visibility: hidden in CSS); opening moves focus to its first link and makes the rest of the page inert; Escape or the burger closes it and returns focus to the burger. The overlay is aria-hidden.
- usage:

```html
<header class="org-site-header"><a class="org-site-header__brand" href="/">SYX</a><nav class="org-site-header__nav" aria-label="Main navigation"><a href="/docs">Docs</a><a href="/themes">Themes</a></nav><div class="org-site-header__actions"><button class="org-site-header__burger" type="button" aria-controls="site-nav-drawer" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Open navigation"><span class="org-site-header__burger-line" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="org-site-header__burger-line" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="org-site-header__burger-line" aria-hidden="true"></span></button></div></header><div class="org-site-nav-overlay" aria-hidden="true"></div><nav class="org-site-nav-drawer" id="site-nav-drawer" aria-label="Mobile navigation"><a class="org-site-nav-drawer__link" href="/docs">Docs</a><a class="org-site-nav-drawer__link" href="/themes">Themes</a></nav>
```

### `org-site-nav-drawer`
[scope: domain-reusable] Mobile-first sticky header with a hamburger that opens a nav drawer over an overlay. The header, drawer and overlay are three sibling elements and all three must be present; the burger names the drawer with aria-controls. js/syx-site-nav.js (no dependencies) toggles [data-nav-open] on <body> and manages focus and inert. The __theme-select and __darkmode controls are documentation-site furniture — a product that ships no theme picker should drop them rather than hide them.
- elements: `org-site-nav-drawer__link` `org-site-nav-drawer__theme`
- states: `.is-scrolled` `:focus-visible` `:hover`
- composed of: `atom-btn` `atom-icon` `atom-select`
- a11y: <header> with a labelled desktop <nav> and a separately labelled drawer <nav>. Burger: <button type="button"> with aria-controls (drawer id), aria-expanded and aria-label. js/syx-site-nav.js: closed drawer is inert (and visibility: hidden in CSS); opening moves focus to its first link and makes the rest of the page inert; Escape or the burger closes it and returns focus to the burger. The overlay is aria-hidden.
- usage:

```html
<header class="org-site-header"><a class="org-site-header__brand" href="/">SYX</a><nav class="org-site-header__nav" aria-label="Main navigation"><a href="/docs">Docs</a><a href="/themes">Themes</a></nav><div class="org-site-header__actions"><button class="org-site-header__burger" type="button" aria-controls="site-nav-drawer" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Open navigation"><span class="org-site-header__burger-line" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="org-site-header__burger-line" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="org-site-header__burger-line" aria-hidden="true"></span></button></div></header><div class="org-site-nav-overlay" aria-hidden="true"></div><nav class="org-site-nav-drawer" id="site-nav-drawer" aria-label="Mobile navigation"><a class="org-site-nav-drawer__link" href="/docs">Docs</a><a class="org-site-nav-drawer__link" href="/themes">Themes</a></nav>
```

## Tokens your app may read

Read these in `--pigmento-*` token declarations. Never read `--primitive-*` or `--component-*` from app code,
and never declare a new name under these prefixes: your tokens are `--pigmento-*`.
